heading, Spill's employee assistance programme (EAP) for residential care homes, level 1

The early shift starts before sunrise, and the rota never quite has enough names on it. Care home staff give residents everything, then lose them, and often grieve on the job because there's no time to grieve off it. Spill gives your team same-day therapy that fits around shifts, with counsellors who specialise in grief and compassion fatigue. Booking a session takes one click from a phone, and you can be up and running in hours, not months.
heading, Proudly supporting care home staff across the UK, level 2
heading, Why care home work wears people down, level 2

60% of care staff have experienced burnout or emotional exhaustion. In residential care, the causes are plain to see: round-the-clock rotas that stretch too few people, the loss of residents they've grown close to, and understaffing that turns every shift into a sprint.
60% of care staff have experienced burnout or emotional exhaustion.
57% of carers feel overwhelmed because they can't switch off from work.
61% of carers worry about their finances and struggle to make ends meet.

navigation, What's the best EAP for residential care homes?

A care home should judge an EAP on three things: whether staff on earlies, lates and nights can actually get appointments, whether counsellors specialise in grief and compassion fatigue, and whether caps or exclusions will shut out the people struggling most. Spill offers unlimited same-day sessions from 7am to 9:30pm, seven days a week, bookable by SMS or email as well as Slack and MS Teams, with counsellors in the top 5% nationally. Nobody is excluded for pre-existing or severe cases, and it's the UK's highest rated EAP on Trustpilot. Traditional helpline EAPs cost less, and that's their honest appeal, but 6 to 8 session caps and call centre access keep usage at 3 to 5%, which helps nobody on your rota.
end of navigation, What's the best EAP for residential care homes?

end of button, How does working in residential care homes affect mental health?, 1 control, not expanded, has popup menu
navigation, How does working in residential care homes affect mental health?

Care home work combines physical graft, emotional closeness and repeated loss, on rotas that rarely have slack. When a resident dies, staff are expected to carry on with the next round of care. It's no surprise that 60% of care staff have experienced burnout or emotional exhaustion. Left unsupported, that exhaustion becomes sickness, turnover and thinner rotas still. Same-day therapy interrupts the cycle while it's still interruptible.
end of navigation, How does working in residential care homes affect mental health?

navigation, What languages do you cover?

Spill offers therapy sessions in 15+ languages, so your team can speak freely with a counsellor that understands them best. Employees choose their preferred language from a drop-down when they book a session. We currently cover Armenian, Croatian, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Igbo, Italian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Slovenian, Spanish, Tagalog and Ukrainian. We're adding to this list all the time, so let us know if you have a request.

navigation, Is Spill compliant with UK data protection and GDPR requirements for care employers?

Yes, Spill operates in compliance with GDPR and UK data protection law. Spill is fully secure and therapy sessions are strictly confidential. Video sessions run on an end-to-end encrypted service and all messages to and from therapists are secure. We share aggregate usage data with the company (the number of people who have used Spill) but never names. Slack and MS Teams are only portals used to sign in to our confidential platform. No session content is ever visible to them, to Spill, or to your company.
end of navigation, Is Spill compliant with UK data protection and GDPR requirements for care employers?
